plainEnglish.summary: Every image, icon, chart, or visual element carrying meaning must have a text description so blind users and screen readers understand what is on screen.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen readers cannot interpret pixel graphics. Text descriptions (alt text) turn visuals into spoken words or braille outputs.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A shopping cart button represented only by an icon must have alt text or aria-label set to 'Shopping Cart (3 items)'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Specify alternative text for key visuals and mark decorative background flourishes as decorative (alt="").
personaBreakdown.developer: Add descriptive alt attributes to tags. Use alt="" or aria-hidden="true" for purely decorative graphics.
personaBreakdown.qa: Use axe-core or browser DevTools to inspect missing alt attributes and verify screen reader announcements on visual controls.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Ensure content creators write alt text for hero banners, infographics, and chart figures in CMS inputs.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core image-alt rule flags missing alt attributes.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure non-text buttons receive focus and display visible focus indicators.
testingGuide.screenReader: Navigate with VoiceOver or NVDA. Confirm screen reader speaks the purpose of the image.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 breaks non-text content into distinct functional outcomes: interactive element naming, media alternatives, and detectable text.

plainEnglish.summary: Prerecorded audio files (podcasts) need transcripts, and prerecorded silent videos need text or audio descriptions.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Deaf users cannot hear audio podcasts; blind users cannot see silent video content.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A podcast player provides a link to a full text transcript directly below the player controls.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design layout slots for text transcripts next to media players.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide accessible transcript containers and link text files to media players.
personaBreakdown.qa: Verify that transcripts accurately represent all spoken content and key sound effects.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Budget for transcript generation in media production workflows.

testingGuide.automated: Manual inspection required for transcript accuracy.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure transcript toggle buttons are keyboard accessible.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader can read the transcript content line by line.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: Read full transcript of Podcast Episode 4
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <audio src="podcast.mp3" controls></audio> <!-- No transcript provided -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 unifies media alternatives into controllable media alternative outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Prerecorded video with spoken audio must have synchronized captions.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users rely on captions to follow video dialogue and sound effects.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A YouTube product video includes closed captions (CC) synchronized with dialogue.

personaBreakdown.designer: Ensure video player UI includes a prominent CC toggle button.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide WebVTT caption tracks via the HTML5 <track kind="captions"> tag.
personaBreakdown.qa: Watch videos with audio muted and confirm captions match speech accurately.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require synchronized captioning for all published video marketing assets.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core video-caption rule checks for <track> elements.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure CC button can be toggled via keyboard.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader announces caption track status.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <video src="promo.mp4" controls></video>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes captions in comprehensive media accessibility outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Prerecorded videos must provide an audio description or full text transcript describing visual actions.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Blind users miss crucial visual-only context in videos (such as text on screen or silent action sequences).
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A video demonstration includes a secondary audio track describing visual steps on screen.

personaBreakdown.designer: Account for audio description toggle options in custom video players.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement secondary audio tracks or detailed text description alternatives.
personaBreakdown.qa: Listen to audio description tracks to verify visual scenes are adequately described.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Plan for audio description recording during video editing.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure audio description channel toggles are keyboard operable.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify description track status announcements.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <video src="demo.mp4"></video>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates audio description into media outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Live streaming video with audio must have live synchronized captions.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Deaf users participating in live webinars, broadcasts, or meetings need real-time captions.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A live corporate webcast uses real-time CART captioners to display live subtitles.

personaBreakdown.designer: Reserve UI space on live video players for real-time text overlays.
personaBreakdown.developer: Integrate live WebSockets/WebRTC caption streams into video player components.
personaBreakdown.qa: Monitor live streams and confirm latency of live captions remains minimal.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Hire live CART captioning services for major live events.

testingGuide.automated: Manual verification during live broadcast required.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure live caption toggle controls are keyboard accessible.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify live caption aria-live region announcements.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: [Speaker]: Welcome to the webcast
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <video id="live-stream"></video> <!-- No live captions -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maintains live captioning as a key media requirement.

plainEnglish.summary: Prerecorded video content must provide audio descriptions for visual information.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Ensures blind viewers understand on-screen visual details that aren't spoken in the main soundtrack.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A movie stream provides a dedicated 'English - Audio Description' soundtrack option.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design audio track selection controls in video player settings.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide multi-audio track selection using HTML5 media API.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test video playback with the AD track enabled.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce audio description requirements across video library publishing.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify audio track selection dropdown is keyboard operable.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader announces selected audio track.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <video src="video.mp4"></video>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 1.2.5 to media alternative guidelines.

plainEnglish.summary: Visual structures like headers, lists, form fields, and table headers must be coded in semantic HTML so screen readers understand relationships.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Sighted users see visual cues like bold text for headings or indentation for lists. Screen reader users rely on semantic HTML elements (<h1>, <ul>, <fieldset>, <th>) to perceive those exact relationships.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Form fields styled to look like a group must use <fieldset> and <legend> so screen readers announce group context.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design logical heading hierarchies (H1 -> H2 -> H3) and clear form groupings.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use standard HTML5 semantic elements (<h1>-<h6>, <nav>, <main>, <fieldset>, <th>, <ul>) rather than generic styled <div> elements.
personaBreakdown.qa: Inspect page structure with HTML Headings Browser extensions or DOM inspection. Ensure table headers use <th>.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Avoid mixing heading hierarchy levels in design systems.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core checks for skipped heading levels, orphaned form labels, and table header issues.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify DOM tab order matches visual layout flow.
testingGuide.screenReader: Press 'H' in NVDA/JAWS to navigate headings; press 'T' to navigate table headers.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad:
Billing Address
Street Address

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 separates structural relationships into component-level information and process-level semantic hierarchy.

plainEnglish.summary: The reading order in the underlying code (DOM) must match the visual logical order of the content.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen readers read content in DOM order. If CSS positioning moves visual text around out of order, screen reader users hear confusing, jumbled sentences.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A multi-column article layout reads column 1 top-to-bottom, then column 2, matching DOM structure.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design linear content layouts that translate cleanly to single-column reading orders.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid using CSS flexbox `order` or `absolute` positioning to rearrange content out of logical reading sequence.
personaBreakdown.qa: Disable CSS styles and verify that the unstyled text flows logically from top to bottom.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Ensure content structure specs maintain sequential logic.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through content and verify focus moves logically.
testingGuide.screenReader: Listen to continuous screen reader reading (NVDA Insert+Down Arrow).
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <!-- CSS flex order reverses DOM sequence confusing screen readers -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 links meaningful sequence to layout reflow and visual presentation outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Instructions must not rely solely on shape, color, size, visual location, or sound (e.g., 'click the round green button on the right').
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Blind users cannot see 'green' or 'round'; screen reader users do not experience spatial locations like 'on the right'.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Instructions say 'Click the green Submit button (marked with a checkmark icon)', combining color with text and icon details.

personaBreakdown.designer: Pair spatial or color cues with explicit text labels.
personaBreakdown.developer: Ensure button labels contain clear descriptive text rather than relying on location context.
personaBreakdown.qa: Verify that instructions remain clear when viewed in greyscale or plain text.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Audit copywriting for spatial or sensory assumptions.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure identified controls are keyboard focusable.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify instructions make sense when read out of visual context.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <!-- Instructions say: Click the blue circle on the right -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates sensory independence into clear language and control information.

plainEnglish.summary: Content must not lock display orientation to portrait or landscape unless essential.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with mobile devices mounted on wheelchairs cannot rotate their screens.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A banking app works seamlessly in both portrait and landscape orientation on tablets and smartphones.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design responsive layouts for both portrait and landscape viewports.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid CSS or JS orientation locks (`screen.orientation.lock('portrait')`).
personaBreakdown.qa: Rotate test devices and confirm layout adjusts without losing content or functionality.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require dual-orientation support in mobile project acceptance criteria.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Test tabbing in both portrait and landscape modes.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify layout reflows without breaking accessibility tree.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Forcing portrait mode via JS lock on load */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 carries orientation support forward into minimum and enhanced viewport outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Form inputs collecting personal user info must use standard HTML `autocomplete` attributes so browsers can auto-fill data.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with cognitive disabilities or motor impairments struggle to manually type personal details like address, name, or email.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: An email input field uses `autocomplete="email"`, allowing browsers to automatically populate the user's stored email.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design standard form fields for user data collection.
personaBreakdown.developer: Add correct HTML5 `autocomplete` attributes (e.g. `name`, `email`, `street-address`, `tel`).
personaBreakdown.qa: Test form fields with browser autofill features.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce standard autocomplete attributes in design systems.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify browser autofill menu triggers cleanly on keyboard focus.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader announces field purpose.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <input type="text" id="field1"> <!-- Missing autocomplete -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 expands autocomplete into automated entry and redundant entry outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Color must not be the only visual indicator used to convey information, indicate an action, or prompt a response.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Color-blind users (red-green, blue-yellow) cannot distinguish status changes signaled only by color changes.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Form error fields display a red border AND an alert icon with error text 'Email is required'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Pair color indicators with text labels, underline styles, or icons.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use text messages and distinct border/icon patterns alongside color changes.
personaBreakdown.qa: View pages in greyscale (using Chrome DevTools color filter) and verify all information remains clear.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce multi-cue design requirements in brand guidelines.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core flags links inside body text that rely solely on color without underlines.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect focused elements for non-color focus indicators.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader receives status announcements.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: Read More

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates use of color rules into distinguishable component outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: If audio plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, a mechanism must be available to pause, stop, or control the volume independently.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Autoplay audio drowns out screen reader speech, making it impossible for blind users to navigate the page.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A website background video plays silently by default and offers an explicit Mute/Play sound button.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design prominent pause/mute controls for background media.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid audio autoplay. If unavoidable, provide keyboard-accessible mute controls at top of page.
personaBreakdown.qa: Load pages with audio and verify pause buttons work immediately.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Prohibit autoplay background audio in site specifications.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core video-autoplay rule checks media tags.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Press Tab to reach the audio pause button immediately on load.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader user can mute background audio instantly.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <audio src="music.mp3" autoplay></audio> <!-- No pause control -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 categorizes audio control under user media control outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Text must have enough color contrast against its background (at least 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Low contrast text is unreadable for people with low vision or under bright sunlight.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Dark grey text (#333333) on white background (#FFFFFF) achieves a 12.6:1 contrast ratio.

personaBreakdown.designer: Select text color palettes that pass 4.5:1 contrast using Figma plugins.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement compliant CSS color tokens. Avoid low-opacity text on light backgrounds.
personaBreakdown.qa: Use Chrome DevTools Color Picker to measure contrast ratios.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce contrast ratio requirements in design tokens.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core color-contrast audit flags non-compliant ratios.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure contrast holds true for :focus and :hover states.
testingGuide.screenReader: Visual check for sighted screen magnifier users.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: .text-body { color: #a0aec0; background-color: #ffffff; } /* 2.3:1 */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 transitions to advanced visual perceptual algorithms (APCA).

plainEnglish.summary: Text must be resizable up to 200% using browser zoom without loss of content or functionality.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with low vision enlarge browser font size to read text without using a screen magnifier.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A news article scales cleanly up to 200% zoom without horizontal scrolling or text clipping.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design flexible container layouts that accommodate larger text sizes.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use relative CSS units (`rem`, `em`, `%`) rather than fixed pixel (`px`) heights on containers.
personaBreakdown.qa: Zoom browser to 200% (Ctrl/Cmd + '+') and verify text does not overlap or get cut off.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Include 200% text zoom requirements in QA acceptance criteria.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core meta-viewport rule checks if user scaling is disabled.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify controls remain keyboard accessible at 200% zoom.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader reads expanded text flow.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, user-scalable=no">

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps text resizing to text-size-adjustable outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Use real HTML text instead of images of text (pictures of text) wherever possible.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Images of text pixelate when zoomed, cannot be restyled by users, and fail custom high-contrast modes.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Hero banner titles use styled HTML <h1> elements overlaid on background images rather than baking text into PNG images.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design banners with live web fonts rendered over background images.
personaBreakdown.developer: Render live text styled with CSS typography instead of using flat text images.
personaBreakdown.qa: Highlight text on web banners to confirm it is live selectable text.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require CMS templates to use live web fonts instead of static image banners.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core flags image elements with text-like alt attributes.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect live text elements.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader reads live text naturally.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 requires detectable, selectable text across media.

plainEnglish.summary: Content must reflow into a single column at 400% zoom (viewport width 320px) without forcing 2D scrolling.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Low vision users zooming to 400% should read vertically without scrolling back and forth horizontally for every line.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A 3-column website layout collapses into a single vertical column on narrow or highly zoomed screens.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design responsive single-column layouts for small viewports.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use CSS flexbox/grid and media queries (`@media (max-width: ...)`). Avoid fixed pixel container widths.
personaBreakdown.qa: Zoom browser to 400% at 1280x1024 resolution. Confirm horizontal scrollbar does not appear.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce responsive design standards across all web properties.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through single-column reflow layout.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader reads single-column flow in sequence.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: .container { width: 1280px; } /* Forces horizontal scroll at 400% zoom */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 groups 1.4.10 under layout-reflow-supported outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Visual indicators for interactive controls (buttons, input borders, icons, focus rings) must have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Low vision users cannot locate form inputs or button boundaries if input borders are faint light grey.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Input field borders use dark grey (#767676) against white backgrounds, achieving 4.5:1 contrast.

personaBreakdown.designer: Specify 3:1+ contrast for form borders, UI icons, and focus rings.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use CSS border and stroke colors meeting 3:1 contrast.
personaBreakdown.qa: Use DevTools Color Picker to measure contrast on input borders and custom checkbox frames.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Include UI component contrast specs in design systems.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify focused state border contrast.
testingGuide.screenReader: Visual check for sighted keyboard users.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: input { border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; } /* 1.4:1 contrast - Fails */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 adopts 1.4.11 into interactive-element-contrast-sufficient outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Content must accommodate custom user text spacing (line height 1.5x, paragraph spacing 2x, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em) without breaking layout.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Dyslexic readers apply custom CSS text spacing to improve reading comprehension.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A web app accommodates increased line height and word spacing without text overlapping or overflowing containers.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design card containers with flexible vertical padding.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid setting fixed `height` or `overflow: hidden` on text containers.
personaBreakdown.qa: Apply text spacing bookmarklet CSS override and verify text stays inside containers.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Verify text spacing adaptability in design system testing.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through text-spaced page layout.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader reads text spaced paragraphs cleanly.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: .card { height: 100px; overflow: hidden; } /* Text clips when line height expands */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps text spacing to blocks-of-text-adjustable outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Additional content appearing on hover or focus (tooltips, popovers) must be dismissible, hoverable, and persistent.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Tooltips that disappear when moving the mouse pointer make reading impossible for screen magnifier users.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A tooltip stays open when the user moves the mouse pointer over the tooltip itself and closes when Esc is pressed.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design tooltips that allow pointer interaction without disappearing.
personaBreakdown.developer: Support Escape key dismissal and ensure hover popovers don't hide when mouse moves over popover content.
personaBreakdown.qa: Hover over tooltips, move mouse onto tooltip body, and press Esc to dismiss.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require compliant tooltip library adoption across products.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Press Tab to trigger tooltip; press Escape to dismiss.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader announces tooltip text upon focus.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Tooltip stays open on hover & pointer entry; closes on Escape keydown listener */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Tooltip closes instantly when mouse leaves trigger element before reaching tooltip */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 incorporates hover/focus popovers into notification and state availability outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: All functionality must be usable using only a keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space, Arrows)—no mouse required.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Blind users, motor-impaired users, and power users operate web applications without a mouse.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A modal dialog opens on Enter, receives focus, and closes on Space or Escape key.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design explicit keyboard interactions for custom dropdowns, tabs, and modals.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use native HTML interactive elements (<button>, <a>). For custom widgets, handle keydown events (Enter/Space).
personaBreakdown.qa: Unplug the mouse! Tab through the page and verify every button, link, and modal is reachable and actionable.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require keyboard accessibility specs in acceptance criteria.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core flags onclick handlers on non-interactive elements like <div> without tabindex.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Press Tab to move through controls. Press Enter/Space to trigger actions.
testingGuide.screenReader: Ensure screen reader virtual cursor can activate controls.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: Submit

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 expands keyboard access into comprehensive input operation outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Keyboard focus must never get trapped or stuck inside a component; users must be able to navigate away using Tab or Shift+Tab.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: If focus gets stuck inside a custom text editor or modal widget, keyboard users are completely trapped and must restart their browser.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A modal window allows tabbing through its internal controls and provides an explicit Close button or Escape key exit.

personaBreakdown.designer: Provide clear visible exit controls on all overlay components.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement keyboard focus traps ONLY inside active modal dialogs, and ensure Escape key unlocks focus.
personaBreakdown.qa: Tab into every interactive component, widget, and modal; verify you can tab back out.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Treat keyboard traps as P0 release-blocking bugs.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core traps focus in automated test runs.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab into control, attempt to tab out forwards and backwards (Shift+Tab).
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader cursor is not trapped in iframe or custom widget.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Modal traps focus inside while open, but pressing Esc or Close returns focus to trigger button */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Focus enters custom widget and Tab key ceases to work anywhere on page */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 addresses keyboard traps under task completion and navigation provisions.

plainEnglish.summary: Single-character keyboard shortcuts (like pressing 'F' to search) must be turn-offable or remappable.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Speech recognition users say 'Find' and speech engines output the letter 'F', triggering unwanted shortcuts randomly.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A web webmail app allows users to disable single-letter shortcuts in settings or requires Ctrl/Cmd modifier keys.

personaBreakdown.designer: Use modifier key combinations (Ctrl + K, Alt + S) for app shortcuts.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide user settings to disable or remap single-letter key listeners.
personaBreakdown.qa: Turn on voice control or type single letters to ensure shortcuts don't fire unexpectedly.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Avoid single-key shortcuts unless user customization options exist.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Press single character keys ('s', 'f', 'm') when focus is not in an input.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify voice command input doesn't trigger rogue application shortcuts.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Shortcut requires Ctrl+K instead of plain 'K' */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Document keydown listener fires global action on single keypress 'F' */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 categorizes shortcut controls under user control outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Users must be given options to turn off, adjust, or extend time limits on pages.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with reading, cognitive, or physical disabilities need extra time to complete forms or read content.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A session timeout warning popup appears 2 minutes before expiration asking 'Do you need more time?'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include session extension warnings in user interface flows.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement timeout extension modals with at least a 20-minute window or simple extend button.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test session timeouts and verify the extension dialog opens and extends the session cleanly.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Set default session timeouts to maximum allowable security limits.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Ensure 'Extend Session' button in timeout warning modal is focused automatically.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader announces session warning (aria-live="assertive").
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Silent 5-minute session timeout redirects user losing all form data */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 moves timing controls to 'no-artificial-time-limits' under process completion.

plainEnglish.summary: Moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating content lasting >5 seconds must have controls to pause, stop, or hide it.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Moving carousels and animated tickers severely distract users with ADHD or cognitive impairments.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A homepage carousel slider includes a visible Pause/Play button.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include a visible Pause button on all auto-rotating carousels and animated banners.
personaBreakdown.developer: Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS media query and provide explicit pause JS controls.
personaBreakdown.qa: Verify carousels stop moving when Pause is clicked or when mouse hovers over slide.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Prohibit auto-playing carousels without pause buttons.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab to Pause button and press Space to halt motion.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader user can pause live tickers.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Auto-advancing image slider with no pause button */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 handles moving content under animation-and-movement outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Web pages must not contain content that flashes more than three times per second to prevent seizures.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Rapidly flashing content can trigger photosensitive epileptic seizures.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Video elements and animations are audited to ensure flash rates remain below 3Hz.

personaBreakdown.designer: Avoid strobe effects or rapid flashing animations in video or UI transitions.
personaBreakdown.developer: Audit video files with PEAT (Photosensitive Epilepsy Analysis Tool).
personaBreakdown.qa: Run PEAT tool on video marketing content before publishing.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Ban flashing animations in creative briefs.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Visual inspection.
testingGuide.screenReader: N/A directly; critical for physical user health.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Smooth CSS fade transition (0.3s) instead of rapid flash */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Rapid strobe effect flashing red/white 5 times a second */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maintains seizure prevention as a core health requirement.

plainEnglish.summary: Provide a mechanism (like a 'Skip to main content' link) to bypass repeated header/navigation blocks.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Keyboard and screen reader users should not have to tab through 50 top menu links on every page refresh.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Tabbing at the top of a page reveals a 'Skip to content' button that jumps focus directly to <main>.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design visible skip link styling when focused.
personaBreakdown.developer: Add `Skip to content` as the first element in .
personaBreakdown.qa: Press Tab immediately on page load and confirm Skip Link appears and moves focus to main content.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce skip link implementation across site templates.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core skip-link rule checks for bypass mechanism.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Press Tab on fresh page load, press Enter on skip link, verify focus lands on <main>.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader announces skip link as first focusable item.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <!-- Page header has 60 links and no skip link -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 groups skip links under navigating-content guidelines.

plainEnglish.summary: Web pages must have descriptive, unique `<title>` tags.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen reader users and browser tab users rely on title tags to know which page or app view is active.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: The checkout page title reads 'Checkout - Step 2: Shipping | Acme Store'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Define page title naming conventions for user journeys.
personaBreakdown.developer: Dynamically set `<title>` tags on route changes in single-page apps (SPAs).
personaBreakdown.qa: Navigate through site pages and verify browser tab title updates accurately.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Include descriptive title tag requirements in SEO & a11y specs.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core document-title rule checks for non-empty <title>.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect document title in browser tab.
testingGuide.screenReader: Screen reader speaks page title upon navigation.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <title>Document</title>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 incorporates page titles into navigation structure outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Keyboard focus navigation order (Tab sequence) must preserve logical meaning and operability.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: If tabbing jumps randomly around the page, keyboard users lose track of visual context.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Tabbing moves from form field 1 -> field 2 -> field 3 -> Submit button in natural sequence.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design logical layout reading paths.
personaBreakdown.developer: Match DOM node order to visual layout flow. Avoid positive `tabindex` values (tabindex="1").
personaBreakdown.qa: Tab through the entire page from top to bottom and verify focus indicator moves sequentially.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Reject layouts that require positive tabindex hacks.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core tabindex rule checks for positive tabindex values.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through page and track outline movement.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm focus sequence matches logical reading order.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <input id="a" tabindex="3"><input id="b" tabindex="1">

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 aligns focus order with navigating-content outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: The purpose of each link must be understandable from its text alone or from its immediate context.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen reader users browse links out of context via a 'Links List' dialog. Vague links like 'Click Here' or 'Read More' become useless.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Link text reads 'Read full WCAG 3 report' instead of just 'Click Here'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Write explicit link text that describes the destination.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use descriptive link text or aria-label (e.g. `aria-label="Read more about Q3 Financials"`).
personaBreakdown.qa: Open screen reader Links List (NVDA Insert+F7) and review link text clarity.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Prohibit vague 'Click Here' copy in content style guides.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core link-name rule flags empty or vague links.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through links and inspect text.
testingGuide.screenReader: Open Links List in NVDA/JAWS and verify destinations make sense.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: Click Here

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 handles link purpose under interactive-element-names-available outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Headings and form labels must be clear, descriptive, and accurately label the content or inputs.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Clear headings allow users to scan pages efficiently; clear labels prevent form input errors.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A form uses specific field labels like 'Mobile Phone Number' instead of generic 'Phone'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Create descriptive heading and form label typography.
personaBreakdown.developer: Associate `<label for="...">` tags explicitly with form input IDs.
personaBreakdown.qa: Review heading titles and form labels for clarity and conciseness.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce consistent copywriting across form fields.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core label-title-only rule checks for missing label text.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Click labels to verify focus transfers to form inputs.
testingGuide.screenReader: Screen reader announces label when input gains focus.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: Phone:

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 2.4.6 to process instructions and control naming.

plainEnglish.summary: Any keyboard-operable interface must have a clearly visible focus indicator when selected.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Without a visual focus outline, keyboard users cannot see where they are on screen when tabbing.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A solid blue ring or high-contrast border appears around a button when focused via Tab key.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design high-contrast focus rings for light and dark themes.
personaBreakdown.developer: Never set `outline: none` without providing a robust `:focus-visible` custom style.
personaBreakdown.qa: Tab through all interactive controls and verify focus outline is bright and unobstructed.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Reject designs or PRs that hide focus outlines for aesthetic reasons.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core flags outline:0 or outline:none without focus overrides.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through page elements and inspect visual outline clarity.
testingGuide.screenReader: N/A directly; visual focus is vital for sighted keyboard users.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: button:focus { outline: none; }

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 provides quantitative metrics for focus area size and contrast ratio.

plainEnglish.summary: New in WCAG 2.2! Focus indicators must be large enough and have sufficient contrast against adjacent colors.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Faint 1px grey focus dots are technically 'visible' under 2.4.7, but fail 2.4.11 because low vision users miss them.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Focus indicators must have an area of at least 1-pixel thickness around the element periphery and 3:1 contrast.

personaBreakdown.designer: Specify 2px+ thick focus outlines with distinct contrast relative to adjacent background colors.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use standard `outline` or `box-shadow` CSS rules with at least 2px thickness.
personaBreakdown.qa: Measure focus indicator dimensions and contrast against background colors.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Ensure design tokens include standardized focus indicators passing WCAG 2.2 AA.

testingGuide.automated: Manual element inspector check in DevTools recommended.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through elements and visually confirm focus outline contrast and thickness.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify focus announcements match focused controls.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: button:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #cccccc; } /* Too faint */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 builds directly on 2.4.11's quantitative focus measurement rules.

plainEnglish.summary: The accessible name (for speech recognition & screen readers) must contain the text presented visually on screen.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Voice control users say 'Click Submit'. If visual text says 'Submit' but aria-label says 'Send Form', voice activation fails.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A button visually displaying 'Search' must have an accessible name starting with 'Search'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Ensure visual label text matches intended functionality.
personaBreakdown.developer: Make sure `aria-label` includes the exact text visible inside the button/control.
personaBreakdown.qa: Compare visual label text with DOM accessible name in Chrome DevTools Accessibility tree.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Maintain label consistency across UI copies and aria annotations.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect DOM accessible name via DevTools.
testingGuide.screenReader: Test voice activation (e.g. Voice Control or Dragon NaturallySpeaking).
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <button aria-label="Find Items">Search</button>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 carries this requirement forward directly as 'label-included-in-programmatic-name'.

plainEnglish.summary: New in WCAG 2.2! Any functionality requiring a dragging movement (drag-and-drop, sliders) must have a single-pointer alternative.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with motor tremors or operating eye-gaze tracking cannot perform smooth click-and-drag mouse movements.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A kanban board allowing drag-and-drop card moves also provides a 'Move to Column...' dropdown button menu.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design tap/click button alternatives alongside drag-and-drop UI interactions.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide click-based button controls (e.g. Move Up / Move Down buttons) next to drag handles.
personaBreakdown.qa: Attempt to operate drag-and-drop interfaces using single mouse clicks or spacebar keypresses.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require single-pointer button alternatives for all drag-and-drop features.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify single-pointer buttons receive focus and trigger moves.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader users can trigger card movements via menu buttons.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Drag handle is the ONLY way to reorder item on page */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 incorporates single-pointer alternatives under pointer input operation outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: New in WCAG 2.2! Interactive targets (buttons, links) must be at least 24x24 CSS pixels or have sufficient spacing around them.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: People with hand tremors or using smartphones can easily mis-tap small, cramped buttons placed right next to each other.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Inline icons or small buttons are given padding/margin so the touch region spans at least 24x24px.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design touch targets to at least 24x24px (44x44px recommended for mobile).
personaBreakdown.developer: Use CSS `min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px;` or padding to expand click areas.
personaBreakdown.qa: Inspect touch target size in DevTools for desktop and mobile viewports.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Include target size minimums in mobile design guidelines.

testingGuide.automated: Lighthouse mobile audit flags cramped tap targets.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect element bounding rect in Chrome DevTools.
testingGuide.screenReader: N/A directly; vital for touch and pointer users.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: .icon-btn { width: 12px; height: 12px; padding: 0; }

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 incorporates touch target metrics into comprehensive pointer control guidelines.

plainEnglish.summary: The default human language of each web page must be specified in HTML (`<html lang="en">`).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen readers use the `lang` attribute to choose correct pronunciation rules, voice synthesizers, and accents.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: An English site sets `<html lang="en-US">`, allowing screen readers to speak in an American English voice.

personaBreakdown.designer: Specify target page languages in site architecture docs.
personaBreakdown.developer: Set valid ISO language codes in the `<html lang="...">` attribute on every page.
personaBreakdown.qa: Inspect DOM source code and verify `lang` attribute is present on `<html>`.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce `lang` attribute inclusion in template headers.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect html element attribute.
testingGuide.screenReader: Listen to screen reader pronunciation when page loads.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <html> <!-- Missing lang attribute -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 3.1.1 directly to human-language-detectable.

plainEnglish.summary: The human language of any passage or phrase in a page that differs from default language must be specified in code (`<span lang="fr">`).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Without `lang="fr"`, an English screen reader will pronounce French words using harsh English phonetics.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample:
A French quote inside an English article uses `
C'est la vie
`.

personaBreakdown.designer: Flag foreign phrases in content editor style guides.
personaBreakdown.developer: Wrap foreign phrases in `span` or `div` elements with valid `lang` attributes.
personaBreakdown.qa: Listen to screen reader pronunciation when reaching foreign quotes.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require CMS support for inline language tagging.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core valid-lang rule checks inline lang tags.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect inline element attributes.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader switches voice engine accent for foreign phrase.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: She said Bonjour to everyone.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes inline language in human-language-detectable outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Receiving keyboard focus on a component must not automatically trigger a change of context (like submitting a form or opening a new page).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Tabbing through a form should never automatically submit data or jump to another URL without user confirmation.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Focusing an input field displays helper text below it, but does NOT submit the form or open a pop-up window.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design predictable form focus behavior.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid attaching navigation or form submit triggers to `onfocus` events.
personaBreakdown.qa: Tab through all form fields and controls; confirm no unexpected page jumps or modal popups occur.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Ban automatic navigation on focus in product requirements.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core checks for onfocus handlers causing context changes.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through elements and monitor window location.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify focus announcements remain predictable.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Focus displays subtle outline; action requires Enter/Space keypress */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <input onfocus="window.location.href='next.html'">

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 categorizes 3.2.1 under change-of-focus-notified outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Changing the setting of any user interface component must not automatically cause a change of context unless informed in advance.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Selecting a checkbox or radio button shouldn't suddenly navigate to a new page without warning.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A country select dropdown updates state silently; a separate 'Filter Results' button submits the change.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include explicit 'Apply' or 'Submit' buttons for dropdown and radio selections.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid triggering `location.href` or major layout replacements on `onchange` events without user warning.
personaBreakdown.qa: Select options in dropdowns and checkboxes; verify context doesn't jump unexpectedly.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce explicit submit actions for major filter controls.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Use arrow keys to select dropdown options; confirm page doesn't submit automatically.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader receives prior warning if input triggers context change.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <select onchange="this.form.submit()"> <!-- Submits form instantly on option hover/arrow -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 addresses 3.2.2 under change-of-content-notified.

plainEnglish.summary: New in WCAG 2.2! Help features (contact info, live chat, FAQ links) appearing on multiple pages must be located in the same relative place.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users seeking help or customer support should find support links in predictable locations across every page.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A 'Contact Support' link is located in the global site footer across all pages.

personaBreakdown.designer: Place help widgets and contact links in standardized global header/footer templates.
personaBreakdown.developer: Include help components inside shared layout wrappers across all routes.
personaBreakdown.qa: Navigate across 5 random site pages and confirm Help/Contact links stay in the exact same relative DOM location.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Standardize support channels in core navigation architecture.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify tab sequence reaches Help link at consistent order across pages.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader users find Help link in consistent nav landmark.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: <!-- Shared Footer template included on all routes contains Help & FAQ links -->
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <!-- Help link placed in header on Page 1, in sidebar on Page 2, and missing on Page 3 -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates 3.2.6 into process instructions and consistency outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: If an input error is automatically detected, the item in error must be identified and the error described to the user in text.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Red borders alone do not tell screen reader or color-blind users which field failed or why.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A failed email field displays text: 'Error: Email address must include an @ symbol'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design error text message callouts directly adjacent to failed input fields.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use `aria-invalid="true"` and connect error text via `aria-describedby="error-id"`.
personaBreakdown.qa: Submit invalid form data and verify error messages are announced by screen readers.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require descriptive validation error messages in form specs.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Submit blank form, tab to invalid input, confirm error text is focused/announced.
testingGuide.screenReader: Screen reader speaks field label AND error description upon focus.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: Please enter a valid email address.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <input class="red-border"> <!-- Color border only, no text error -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 covers error identification under input-constraints-used outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Labels or instructions must be provided when content requires user input.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Without clear labels or format instructions (e.g., 'MM/DD/YYYY'), users guess what data format is expected.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A date input field displays a visible label 'Date of Birth' and format hint '(MM/DD/YYYY)'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include persistent visible labels and format examples for complex input fields.
personaBreakdown.developer: Pair `<label>` elements with inputs and use `aria-describedby` for helper text hints.
personaBreakdown.qa: Inspect form inputs and confirm placeholder text is not used as a substitute for permanent labels.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Prohibit placeholder-only form designs in design reviews.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core label rule checks for missing input labels.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab to field and verify label is spoken.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader announces both label and format instruction text.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: Format: MM/DD/YYYY
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <input placeholder="Date of Birth (MM/DD/YYYY)"> <!-- Placeholder disappears on typing -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 3.3.2 to input constraints and element naming.

plainEnglish.summary: New in WCAG 2.2! Information previously entered by the user in the same process must be automatically populated or available for selection.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Re-typing information like billing/shipping address causes significant cognitive fatigue and errors.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A multi-step checkout form includes a checkbox: 'Same as shipping address'.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include 'Use stored info' or 'Same as...' options in multi-step form designs.
personaBreakdown.developer: Store previous step inputs in state and pre-fill downstream form fields.
personaBreakdown.qa: Complete multi-step form flows and verify user data is auto-populated or easily selectable.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Prioritize seamless data retention across onboarding and checkout funnels.

testingGuide.automated: Manual multi-step form flow test required.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Fill form step 1, advance to step 2, confirm auto-population.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader announces pre-filled input values.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: <label><input type="checkbox" id="same-addr" onclick="copyAddress()"> Billing address same as shipping</label>
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <!-- Forcing manual re-entry of 10 address fields without auto-fill -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 adopts 3.3.7 directly into 'no-redundant-entry' under the retain information group.

plainEnglish.summary: New in WCAG 2.2! Authentication processes must not rely on cognitive function tests (memorizing passwords or solving puzzles) unless alternatives like passkeys or copy-paste exist.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: CAPTCHA puzzles and anti-copy password fields create huge barriers for people with cognitive impairments or dyslexia.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A login form allows users to paste passwords from password managers and supports passkeys/biometrics.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design passwordless login options (passkeys, magic links).
personaBreakdown.developer: Never disable copy-paste (`onpaste="return false"`) on password fields and implement WebAuthn API.
personaBreakdown.qa: Verify password manager auto-fill and copy-pasting work cleanly on login inputs.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Implement modern authentication protocols (WebAuthn / Passkeys).

testingGuide.automated: Check for onpaste="return false" scripts on input fields.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Attempt to copy and paste text into password fields.
testingGuide.screenReader: Test screen reader interaction with authentication prompts.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <input type="password" id="pwd" onpaste="return false;">

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 breaks accessible authentication into cognitive test alternatives, automated entry, and copying support.

plainEnglish.summary: For all custom UI controls, the name (label), role (what component it is), and value/state (expanded, checked, selected) must be programmatically available.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen readers need to know if an element is a button, checkbox, tab, or slider, and whether it is currently checked or expanded.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A custom accordion header uses `role="button"` and `aria-expanded="true"` or `aria-expanded="false"`.

personaBreakdown.designer: Document component states (expanded/collapsed, active/disabled) in component specifications.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use standard HTML elements (<button>, <details>) or appropriate ARIA roles/states (role="tab", aria-selected="true").
personaBreakdown.qa: Inspect accessibility tree in Chrome DevTools or inspect screen reader announcements.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Ensure custom design system components include ARIA accessibility specifications.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core checks for valid ARIA roles, attributes, and values.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Toggle custom controls with Space/Enter and verify state changes.
testingGuide.screenReader: Listen to screen reader output when expanding or checking controls.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: What is WCAG 3?

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 4.1.2 to 'roles-values-states-properties-available'.

plainEnglish.summary: Status messages (success alerts, search result counts) must be announced to assistive tech without receiving focus.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen reader users need to hear '3 results found' or 'Item added to cart' without having their focus focus abruptly moved away from their current input.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A search results count updates dynamically and uses `role="status"` (`aria-live="polite"`).

personaBreakdown.designer: Design non-intrusive status toast and alert regions.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use ARIA live regions (`role="status"` or `role="alert"`) for dynamic content updates.
personaBreakdown.qa: Trigger dynamic updates and verify screen reader speaks the message without moving keyboard focus.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Include live region announcements in dynamic UI specs.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core checks valid ARIA live region attributes.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Trigger action and confirm keyboard focus remains on active input.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader speaks live status message asynchronously.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <!-- Dynamic text updates silently with no ARIA live region -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 handles status messages under changes-to-elements-notified outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Live audio-only broadcasts must provide a live text transcript or live caption stream.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Deaf users listening to live radio or audio webcasts need real-time text descriptions.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A live radio interview stream provides real-time text transcript streaming.

personaBreakdown.designer: Reserve space for live text stream overlays.
personaBreakdown.developer: Connect live speech-to-text API streams to live audio player components.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test live audio streams with real-time text transcription.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Contract live CART transcribers for major live audio broadcasts.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify live transcript toggle is keyboard focusable.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify live transcript aria-live region announcements.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <audio src="live-stream"></audio>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 incorporates live audio alternatives into media outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Where pauses in main video dialogue are insufficient for audio descriptions, provide extended audio descriptions by pausing video playback.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Blind users miss visual storytelling details when dialogue is too fast for standard audio description gaps.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A instructional video automatically pauses visual playback while a narrator describes complex visual steps.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design video player components supporting auto-pausing extended descriptions.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement media player JS event listeners to pause video when playing extended description tracks.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test video playback with extended audio description enabled.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Budget for extended audio description narration.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify extended description toggle is keyboard accessible.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader announces extended description status.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Media player auto-pauses main video track during extended audio narration */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Audio description is truncated because main video track dialogue does not pause */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates extended description into media outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: A full text transcript describing all visual scenes, dialogue, and audio cues must be provided for all prerecorded synchronized media.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Deaf-blind users relying on screen reader braille displays need full descriptive text transcripts of videos.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A video presentation includes a comprehensive text alternative document covering dialogue and visual actions.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include links to full text transcripts next to video embed frames.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide accessible transcript containers and link text files.
personaBreakdown.qa: Read full text transcript while watching video to verify visual details are fully captured.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require full text transcripts for all published media assets.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab to transcript link.
testingGuide.screenReader: Read transcript via braille display or screen reader speech.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <video src="promo.mp4"></video>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps media text alternatives to media alternative outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Text must have an enhanced color contrast ratio of at least 7:1 for normal text and 4.5:1 for large text.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Provides maximum readability for users with severe low vision without requiring screen magnifiers.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: High-contrast black text (#000000) on white background (#FFFFFF) achieves a 21:1 contrast ratio.

personaBreakdown.designer: Select high-contrast color palettes meeting 7:1 ratios.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement high-contrast CSS color variables.
personaBreakdown.qa: Measure contrast using DevTools Color Picker.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce enhanced contrast in accessible design systems.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect focused state contrast.
testingGuide.screenReader: Visual check for low-vision users.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: .text-enhanced { color: #767676; background: #ffffff; } /* 4.5:1 - Passes AA but fails AAA */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 1.4.6 to text-contrast-sufficient-enhanced.

plainEnglish.summary: Background audio under spoken dialogue must be muted by default or at least 20dB lower than speech.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Hard-of-hearing users cannot isolate spoken words when background music or noise is loud.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A video documentary isolates voice narration, turning off background music or reducing it to -20dB.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design audio production specs with separate music and speech tracks.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide multi-track audio selection or clear speech audio streams.
personaBreakdown.qa: Listen to audio track levels with decibel measurement tools.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require low background noise in audio production guidelines.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify audio track selection controls.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify speech clarity.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Background music track is set to -20dB relative to voice track */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Loud background music plays at same volume as speaker voice */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes background audio control under media outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Allow users to customize foreground/background colors, line spacing (1.5x), paragraph spacing (2x), and text width (<80 characters).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Readers with cognitive disabilities or dyslexia require specific layout dimensions and custom color combinations.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A reading app offers a 'Reader View' setting to change background color, line height, and column width.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design customizable typography layouts with max-width 80ch.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid setting fixed container widths and support user CSS custom stylesheets.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test text customization controls in reader settings.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Include Reader View functionality in product specs.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core checks for line-height and max-width metrics.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through reader setting controls.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify text reflows cleanly.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: p { width: 1400px; text-align: justify; } /* Fails AAA visual presentation */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 categorizes 1.4.8 under blocks-of-text-readable-enhanced outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Images of text must not be used under any circumstances except for logos or brand names.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Ensures text is 100% scalable, restylable, and accessible across all assistive technologies.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: All site banners, infographics, and callouts use live HTML text with web fonts.

personaBreakdown.designer: Eliminate static text graphics in favor of live typography.
personaBreakdown.developer: Render all content text using live HTML elements.
personaBreakdown.qa: Select all text on page to verify zero images of text exist.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Prohibit static text graphics across marketing team assets.

testingGuide.automated: axe-core checks image alt text for text duplication.
testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect page elements.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm live text rendering.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 1.4.9 to text-detectable.

plainEnglish.summary: All page functionality must be operable via keyboard without exception (no mouse-only path allowed under any circumstances).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Ensures 100% of features can be activated by keyboard users.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Even complex freehand drawing canvases provide keyboard arrow-key drawing controls.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design keyboard control schemes for 100% of UI interactions.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement keyboard event handlers for all canvas, map, and drawing widgets.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test 100% of site features using only keyboard.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require keyboard parity for all custom widgets.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Test entire application without touching mouse.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader accessibility for all features.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: <canvas tabIndex="0" aria-label="Interactive Canvas (Use arrow keys to draw)"></canvas>
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Canvas drawing features only work on mouse drag */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 builds on complete keyboard operability.

plainEnglish.summary: Content must not have any time limits whatsoever (except for non-interactive live broadcasts).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users can take as long as necessary to read, process, and complete actions without session expiration stress.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Form applications allow users to take hours or days to complete without logging out.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design workflows without session timer indicators.
personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid setting automatic server-side session timeouts.
personaBreakdown.qa: Leave form open for 2 hours and verify data submits successfully without session timeout errors.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Eliminate artificial time limits across customer user journeys.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Verify form remains active over long periods.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm no time limit warnings interrupt reading.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: /* Form data auto-saves and session never expires silently */
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* 10-minute hard timer logs user out without option to extend */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 incorporates 2.2.3 into 'no-artificial-time-limits'.

plainEnglish.summary: Interruptions (like non-emergency popups or alerts) can be postponed or suppressed by the user.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with cognitive disabilities can focus on reading without unexpected popups breaking concentration.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A web app includes a 'Do Not Disturb' toggle that holds all incoming notifications in a inbox queue.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design notification settings controls for holding non-critical alerts.

plainEnglish.summary: Content must not contain any component that flashes more than three times in any one-second period (no exceptions).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Eliminates all seizure risks caused by visual flashing.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: All web animations strictly cap state changes below 2 flashes per second.

personaBreakdown.designer: Ban all flashing transitions in design systems.
personaBreakdown.developer: Enforce smooth CSS transition timing functions.

plainEnglish.summary: Information about the user's location within a set of web pages is available (e.g. breadcrumbs).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Helps users orient themselves within deep hierarchical websites.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A documentation page includes a breadcrumb trail: Home > Docs > WCAG 3 > Guidelines.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include breadcrumb navigation trails on all sub-pages.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement semantic `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"><ol>` lists.

plainEnglish.summary: A mechanism is available to allow the purpose of each link to be identified from link text alone.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users browsing links out of context can understand every link destination without reading surrounding sentences.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Link text reads 'Download Q3 Financial Spreadsheet (XLSX, 2MB)' instead of 'Click Here'.

personaBreakdown.developer: Provide explicit descriptive text inside `<a>` tags.

personaBreakdown.productManager: Enforce self-describing link text in copywriting style guides.

plainEnglish.summary: Section headings are used to organize content into distinct visual and semantic sections.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Break up long walls of text into digestible sections for readers with cognitive impairments.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Every major paragraph section is introduced by a descriptive `<h3>` heading.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design visual section headers for all content blocks.
personaBreakdown.developer: Structure document content using proper heading tags (`<h2>`, `<h3>`).
personaBreakdown.qa: Verify section headings organize all major content blocks.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require section heading structure in editorial specs.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Tab through headings.

plainEnglish.summary: Interactive target size is at least 44x44 CSS pixels (except for inline text links).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Ensures buttons and controls are easily tapable for users with severe hand tremors or motor disabilities.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: All touchscreen buttons and icon controls span at least 44x44px in size.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design interactive targets to at least 44x44px.
personaBreakdown.developer: Apply `min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px;` in CSS.
personaBreakdown.qa: Measure button bounding boxes in Chrome DevTools.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require 44x44px target size across design tokens.

plainEnglish.summary: Provide a mechanism for identifying specific definitions of unusual words, jargon, or idioms.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Helps readers with cognitive disabilities understand specialized terminology.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A technical article includes inline glossary definitions for specialized terms.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design tooltip or inline glossary definition indicators.
personaBreakdown.developer: Use HTML `<dfn>` and definition lists (`<dl>`, `<dt>`, `<dd>`).
personaBreakdown.qa: Test word definition links and glossary tooltips.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Provide glossary terms for technical documentation.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 3.1.3 to clear-language outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Provide a mechanism for identifying the expanded form or definition of abbreviations.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Screen reader users and cognitive readers need to know what acronyms (like W3C or WCAG) stand for.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Abbreviations use `<abbr title="World Wide Web Consortium">W3C</abbr>`.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include abbreviation expansion styling.
personaBreakdown.developer: Wrap acronyms in `<abbr title="...">` tags on first use.
personaBreakdown.qa: Hover over abbreviations and verify title expansion tooltip appears.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require abbreviation definitions in content guidelines.

testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader speaks expanded abbreviation title.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: W3C <!-- Acronym used with no expansion -->

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes abbreviations in clear-language outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: When text requires advanced reading ability beyond lower secondary education level, supplemental clear language versions are available.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Ensures complex medical, legal, or technical documentation can be comprehended by all readers.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A legal terms page includes a 'Plain English Summary' at the top of each section.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design plain-English summary callouts at the top of complex articles.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide simplified text alternatives or toggle views.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test readability score using Flesch-Kincaid grade level analyzers.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require plain English summaries for legal and technical documentation.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect plain English summary callouts.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader reads plain English summaries first.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <!-- Dense 50-page legal text with zero summary -->

plainEnglish.summary: Changes of context are initiated ONLY by user request or a mechanism is available to turn off such changes.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with cognitive disabilities are easily disoriented when pages auto-redirect or refresh automatically.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Selecting an option in a dropdown updates internal state silently without auto-submitting or auto-redirecting.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design explicit submit actions for all form changes.
personaBreakdown.developer: Eliminate automatic page reloads or redirects triggered by selection changes.
personaBreakdown.qa: Select options in dropdowns; confirm page never auto-submits.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Prohibit auto-submitting inputs.

testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm context remains stable.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 3.2.5 to change-of-content-notified outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Context-sensitive help is available for complex form fields.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Provides immediate guidance for users filling out complex financial or tax forms.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Next to a 'Tax ID' field, a tooltip button 'What is this?' opens explicit instructions.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design context-sensitive help icons and modal popovers.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide `aria-describedby` links to contextual help dialogs.
personaBreakdown.qa: Click help icons next to form fields and verify guidance text appears.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require context-sensitive help on complex input workflows.

plainEnglish.summary: For ALL web forms submitting user data, submissions are reversible, verified, or confirmed before final submission.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Prevents accidental data loss or irreversible errors across all form submissions.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Before submitting any form, a confirmation modal displays a summary of entered data for review.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design confirmation review steps for all forms.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement confirmation review screens before processing data writes.
personaBreakdown.qa: Submit forms and confirm review step allows editing data before final submit.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require review/confirmation steps across all application forms.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 covers error prevention under going-back-supported and progress-saved outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Live audio-only content provides a live text alternative (such as real-time CART captions or live transcript text).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Deaf users listening to live radio webcasts or press conferences need live text representations.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A live audio broadcast stream displays an integrated live text transcript feed.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design live transcript overlay containers for live audio players.
personaBreakdown.developer: Stream CART or live speech-to-text API outputs into live `aria-live="polite"` containers.

testingGuide.screenReader: Verify aria-live region updates speak live transcript text.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: <audio src="live-broadcast"></audio>

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates live audio alternatives into media outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: In content implemented using markup languages, the purpose of UI components and icons can be programmatically determined.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Allows assistive tools to substitute standard icons (like a home icon) with personalized symbol sets for users with cognitive or speech disabilities.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Navigation links use standard microdata or HTML autocomplete/purpose attributes allowing custom symbol overlays.

personaBreakdown.designer: Use consistent icon semantics across UI design components.
personaBreakdown.developer: Annotate UI controls with standard microdata/ARIA purpose attributes.
personaBreakdown.qa: Inspect markup for standardized purpose attributes.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Specify symbol-overlay compatibility in design system specs.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Inspect navigation element markup.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader identifies element purpose.
testingGuide.codeSnippetGood: Home

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maps 1.3.6 to element identification and name outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: When an authenticated session expires, the user can continue the activity without loss of data after re-authenticating.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users who take extra time to complete forms due to motor or cognitive disabilities do not lose their typed work if logged out.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A banking session times out, but after logging back in, the user's filled-out wire transfer form is completely restored.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design re-authentication modal dialogs that preserve current page state.
personaBreakdown.developer: Store form state locally in encrypted sessionStorage during re-auth.
personaBreakdown.qa: Let session expire while filling out form, log back in, and verify data remains intact.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require state preservation across re-authentication flows.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Test re-authentication modal using keyboard.
testingGuide.screenReader: Verify screen reader announces saved state restoration.
