testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Session expires and redirects to home page, wiping 30 minutes of typed form data */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 handles re-authentication under progress-saved outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Users are warned about the duration of any user inactivity that could cause data loss.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Prevents surprise session expirations for users taking extra time to complete forms.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A session timeout modal appears 5 minutes before expiration, explicitly stating 'Your session will expire in 5 minutes due to inactivity.'

personaBreakdown.designer: Design prominent session timeout warning dialogs.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement inactivity timer events that display Accessible Warning Modals before session expiration.
personaBreakdown.qa: Wait for inactivity threshold and verify warning dialog pops up with extension option.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require timeout warnings across all authenticated user workflows.

testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* System times out silently with zero advance warning */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates timeout warnings under time limit outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Motion animation triggered by user interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with vestibular spectrum disorders experience severe nausea or dizziness from parallax scrolling or zoom animations.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A website respects `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` by disabling scroll parallax and hover zoom effects.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design alternative static states for all interaction animations.
personaBreakdown.developer: Wrap all CSS animations in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` media queries.
personaBreakdown.qa: Enable 'Reduce Motion' in OS settings and verify UI animations are suppressed.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require reduced motion compliance in design system animation guidelines.

testingGuide.manualKeyboard: Trigger hover/focus effects with reduced motion enabled.
testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm visual stability.
testingGuide.codeSnippetBad: /* Parallax scrolling animations play regardless of OS motion preferences */

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 maintains motion controls under animation-and-movement outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Provide more than one way to locate a web page within a set of web pages (e.g. site search, sitemap, main navigation).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Different users have different preferences for finding information; some prefer top navigation menus, while others rely on search bars or sitemaps.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A corporate website provides top header navigation menus, a header search input, and a footer sitemap link.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design persistent search bars and sitemap footers across all site layouts.
personaBreakdown.developer: Implement header search inputs and semantic footer sitemap links.
personaBreakdown.qa: Verify users can find pages using both main menu and search/sitemap.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require multi-path navigation across site architecture.

plainEnglish.summary: When an item receives keyboard focus, the item is at least partially visible and not entirely hidden behind sticky headers, banners, or popups.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Keyboard users must see what element is currently focused to navigate confidently.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: When tabbing down a long page, focused links scroll into view below sticky top navigation bars.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design scroll padding for sticky header regions.

plainEnglish.summary: When an item receives keyboard focus, no part of the item is obscured by author-created content (100% of focus box is completely visible).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Provides maximum visibility for keyboard users so zero pixels of the focused element are covered.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A sticky chat widget automatically repositions or hides if keyboard focus lands on a link behind it.

personaBreakdown.designer: Design floating widgets to avoid overlapping focusable elements.
personaBreakdown.developer: Dynamically adjust floating overlay positions on element focus.
personaBreakdown.qa: Tab through all page elements and verify 100% of focused boundary box is visible.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require zero focus obscuration across floating UI components.

plainEnglish.summary: All functionality that operates using multipoint or path-based gestures (like pinch-zoom, swiping, or two-finger drag) can be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with motor disabilities or users using head pointers/eye trackers cannot perform complex multi-finger gestures.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: An interactive map allows two-finger pinch-zooming but ALSO provides accessible '+' and '-' zoom buttons.

personaBreakdown.designer: Include single-tap alternative buttons for all gesture-based controls.
personaBreakdown.developer: Provide click event handlers on visible button controls alongside touch gesture handlers.
personaBreakdown.qa: Test gesture widgets using single mouse clicks or single-finger taps.
personaBreakdown.productManager: Require single-pointer button alternatives for gesture features.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes pointer gesture alternatives under gesture outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: For functionality that can be operated using a single pointer, completion of the function is on the up-event (like mouseup or touchend), or a mechanism is available to abort the function before completion.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Prevents accidental clicks when users accidentally touch an screen element and want to drag their finger away before releasing.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A button action triggers on `click` (mouseup), allowing users to slide off the button to cancel the press.

plainEnglish.summary: Functionality triggered by device motion (like shaking or tilting a phone) can also be operated by conventional user interface components, and motion can be disabled.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users with motor impairments who have mobile devices mounted to wheelchairs cannot shake or tilt their device.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A mobile app allows shaking device to undo typing, but ALSO provides an 'Undo' button and an option to turn off shake-to-undo.

testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm screen reader announces undo button.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 includes motion actuation fallbacks under user-control outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: Web content does not restrict use of input mechanisms available on a device (e.g. allowing users to switch freely between mouse, keyboard, touch, and stylus).
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Users frequently switch between touchscreens, external mice, and keyboards depending on task context.
plainEnglish.realWorldExample: A user tabs using keyboard, then taps a touchscreen button, and then uses a mouse without the app blocking any input mode.

personaBreakdown.developer: Avoid locking input modes based on initial device touch detection.

testingGuide.screenReader: Confirm seamless input switching.

wcag3Mapping.evolutionNote: WCAG 3 integrates input mode flexibility under user-control outcomes.

plainEnglish.summary: A mechanism is available for identifying specific pronunciation of words where meaning is ambiguous without knowing pronunciation.
plainEnglish.whyItMatters: Helps screen readers and cognitive readers pronounce heteronyms correctly (e.g., 'read' past vs present, 'desert' verb vs noun).

plainEnglish.summary: Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple web pages occur in the same relative order each time they are repeated.

plainEnglish.summary: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, the suggestion is provided to the user.

plainEnglish.summary: For web pages that cause legal commitments or financial transactions, submissions are reversible, verified, or confirmed before final submission.

plainEnglish.summary: A cognitive function test (such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle) is not required for any step in an authentication process.

plainEnglish.realWorldExample: Login screen fully supports copy-pasting passwords, browser autofill, and biometrics (Touch ID / Face ID).

plainEnglish.realWorldExample: WCAG 2.2 errata formally retired 4.1.1. Focus on semantic HTML tags and valid ARIA attributes instead.
